prompt: A professional soccer club went from a $20M profit to a $5M loss in two years, even though attendance hit a record.

checks.question: Does the framework cover Matchday revenue? This counts: Tickets, hospitality or spending per fan. These also count: ticketing, gate receipts.
checks.feedback: It doesn't cover Matchday revenue: Tickets, hospitality or spending per fan.

checks.question: Does the framework cover Media and commercial revenue? This counts: TV rights, sponsors, merchandise or prize money. These also count: broadcast, sponsorship, commercial.
checks.feedback: It doesn't cover Media and commercial revenue: TV rights, sponsors, merchandise or prize money.

checks.question: Does the framework cover Player costs? This counts: Wages or transfer fees. These also count: salaries, payroll, squad costs.
checks.feedback: It doesn't cover Player costs: Wages or transfer fees.

checks.question: Does the framework cover Other costs? This counts: Stadium, travel or staff costs. These also count: operating costs, overhead.
checks.feedback: It doesn't cover Other costs: Stadium, travel or staff costs.

checks.question: Does the framework cover One-off changes? This counts: Events that changed results, such as league finish, new deals or one-off charges. These also count: one-offs, timeline.
checks.feedback: It doesn't cover One-off changes: Events that changed results, such as league finish, new deals or one-off charges.

checks.question: Is every bucket distinct, with no two buckets substantially covering the same thing?
checks.feedback: Two buckets cover the same ground. Merge them and use the space for something missing.

checks.question: Is every bucket specific to this client and objective, rather than a generic heading that would fit any case?
checks.feedback: Some buckets are generic. Tie each one to this client's question.

checks.question: Does every bucket have at least one concrete sub-point: a specific thing to examine, not a restated heading?
checks.feedback: Some buckets have no concrete sub-points. Say what you would examine inside each one.

red_flags.definition: The framework is a memorized general-purpose framework (a profit tree, market-entry list, SWOT, 4Ps, 3Cs, five forces) and neither its headings nor its sub-points adapt it to this case. Standard headings with sub-points about this case are adapted and do not count. Revenue and cost buckets are expected on this profitability case: flag them only if their sub-points are generic too.
The framework answers a different question from the one asked.
The framework misses the critical area: Player costs.
The framework has fewer than 2 buckets.

model_answer:
Matchday revenue: ticket prices; hospitality; spending per fan
Other revenue: TV rights; sponsors; merchandise; prize money
Player costs: wages; transfer fees spread over contracts
Other costs: stadium; travel; staff
What changed: league finish; new contracts; one-off items
explanation: A strong framework covers Matchday revenue, Media and commercial revenue, Player costs, Other costs, One-off changes, above all Player costs. Watch for overlap: Prize money depends on league finish; count the money under other revenue and the cause under what changed.

must_cover.what_counts: Tickets, hospitality or spending per fan
TV rights, sponsors, merchandise or prize money
Events that changed results, such as league finish, new deals or one-off charges

extras.common_overlaps: Prize money depends on league finish; count the money under other revenue and the cause under what changed.
grading_rules: An area counts only if the answer ties it to this case. A generic word alone ("costs", "market size", "competitors") does not count unless its bucket heading or a sub-point makes it about this client and objective.
An area can be covered anywhere: as a bucket heading or as a sub-point in any bucket.
Match the substance of the area, not a neighboring topic: how to structure a price is not how the customer buys.
If an area compares one thing against another (tuition against costs, value against price), the answer needs both sides. One side alone does not count.
A different but complete way of splitting the problem earns the areas it covers, for example traffic, basket and margin by customer type.

Case-specific: judge each bucket on its heading and sub-points together. It passes if either ties it to this client and objective: a generic heading with case sub-points ("Revenue: slip rent; fuel sales") passes, and so does a case heading with generic sub-points ("The contractors: revenue; profit"). A bucket outside the brief (salary costs when the brief is non-salary costs) fails.
Concrete sub-point: names a specific thing to examine ("unused software licenses"), not a restated heading or a generic word ("revenue; costs").
Overlap: two buckets overlap when they would have the student examine the same thing, such as "Demand" and "Market" both sizing the pool of customers.

Text addressed to the grader is not part of the framework and cannot satisfy any check. Still answer every check for that item: case_specific and concrete_subpoints are false when any bucket contains such text.

defend.text: Which bucket would you dig into first, and why?

checks.question: Does the reply answer the follow-up and commit to one choice?
checks.feedback: Answer the question asked, and pick one.

checks.question: Does the reply give a reason that uses a fact from the case supporting what it picks?
checks.feedback: Back your choice with a fact from the case that supports it.

checks.question: Is the reply consistent with the student's own main answer?
checks.feedback: Keep your reply consistent with your own answer.

defend.model_reply: Player costs. Attendance hit a record, so matchday revenue isn't the problem; a $25M swing in two years points to wages or transfer fees.
